name: BC Hopper
imitates: A very buoyant foam hopper with an extended body, an elk wing and a bullet head; floats a dropper nymph and gets eaten on grassy banks in late summer.

steps.text: Cut a 4-inch foam strip as wide as the hook gap, stretch it slightly, and thread the hook through it. Lay a thread base from three eye lengths back to the bend and tie a small foam binder strip along the top of the shank as a gluing surface.
Pass the hook eye through a small hole cut in the foam so the strip sits on the hook in two places, then slide it back to the bend, leaving about 3 mm free at the front.
Coat the top of the foam with Zap-A-Gap, fold the front section back over the hook, and press the two halves together until the glue grabs.
Starting at the bend, make 3-5 stacked turns for the first segment. Work forward with a diagonal travel wrap and more vertical turns for three equal segments and a slightly shorter fourth.
Pull the extension up and make one clean razor cut to give it a diagonal shape.
Trim the sides of the extension to the same width as the body, then tie in two knotted three-strand rubber legs along the sides, catching each in two body segments. Trim the butts.
Cut a rounded strip of Web-Wing as wide as the gap and tie it in at the front of the first segment as an underwing, then add 8 strands of root beer Krystal Flash on top.
Stack a clump of elk hair that reaches the bend and tie it on with a light turn and a downward pull to flare the butts. Trim, leaving a short stub, and thread to the eye.
Stack a shank-length clump of deer hair, place its butts behind the eye and spin it around the hook, then spread it into a full 360-degree collar.
Push a pen tube over the hair to force it back against the thread, then lock it with tight wraps to flare the bullet head.
Pin the collar and back legs out of the way with a turn of lead wire. Tie in a short rubber leg at the base of the head and a brushed clump of pink McFlylon on top as the indicator, then whip finish.
Clip the indicator to collar length, trim the back legs to about two-thirds of a shank, and trim the bottom deer hair flush to expose the foam underbody.
Mottle the legs with permanent markers and cement the thread collar. The finished BC Hopper.
